rationale: Registering a font whose bytes are identical to a face already registered under the same family now returns the existing registration instead of decoding the woff2 again and appending a duplicate face. A captured plug-in editor registers its packaged fonts on every editor open, and a variable font captured once per @font-face weight rule named the same file many times, so each open decoded and appended the same faces repeatedly. The registration result, the family a caller asks for, and what a lookup returns are unchanged; no API is added or removed, no authority boundary moves, and no alternate renderer appears. Pulp-only because Pulp still builds and ships this implementation independently and there is no counterpart Vellum commit to backport from.
tests: pulp-test-group-canvas re-registering identical font bytes adds no face and keeps caches valid
